records.name: Tikkun Olam Coordinating Team at Germantown Jewish Centre
records.summary: A volunteer team at Germantown Jewish Centre, a synagogue, that follows up on election security and voter protection. It holds Zoom sessions where people talk through local actions they can take.
records.what_you_do: Share voter education, learn about poll worker and poll watcher roles, and talk through local actions. Members can bring their own ideas.

schedule.text: Sessions are held on Zoom and announced one at a time. No later session was posted when the page was read.

first_step.how: Call the synagogue office at 215.844.1507 or email office@germantownjewishcentre.org to ask about the next election session and how to get the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The session was posted publicly and the office invites calls before visits, but the page does not say whether people who are not members may attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: The last session posted ran on Zoom from 7 to 8:30 pm and was used to review possible actions and plan what neighbors could do next. The page lists no cost and does not say who usually attends.
first_visit_tips: Ask the office whether the next session is open to people who are not members.
Read the four partner groups named on the session page (ACLU PA, Committee of Seventy, Election Protection, Philadelphia Neighborhood Networks) so you know what each one offers.

records.notes: One-off session series, no later date posted. The session page names a personal volunteer email as the RSVP contact; it was left out and the office line is used. Audience kept at public from tier 1, but the page does not say whether non-members may attend, so check with the office before relying on it.

records.name: TILT Institute for the Contemporary Image
records.summary: A photography center in North Philadelphia that runs gallery shows, printing services, artist residencies, and youth education for photographers and image makers at every level.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery, book an individual photo tutorial, use the printing team or the Artist Lab, or ask about the youth programs. The artist residency is paid, but applications were closed when the site was read.

schedule.text: Gallery open Wednesday to Saturday, 12 to 6 pm.

cost.text: TILT offers free programs and exhibitions. Photo tutorials cost $105 to $150 an hour on a sliding scale. Memberships run $60 to $500 a year, or $5 to $40 a month.

first_step.how: Stop by the gallery at 1400 N. American Street, Suite 103, any Wednesday to Saturday between 12 and 6 pm to see the current show.
first_step.basis: The gallery is open to anyone during posted hours and each tutorial has a booking link, but the page does not say beginners are welcome, so it is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: Gallery visits are self-guided: you walk through the exhibitions during open hours at no charge. Tutorials are booked with an instructor in blocks of 1, 1.5, or 2 hours, at $105 to $150 an hour on a sliding scale.
first_visit_tips: Gallery hours are Wednesday to Saturday, 12 to 6 pm, so plan the visit inside those hours.
To book a tutorial, contact Danielle Morris, who handles scheduling, at 215.232.5678.
Membership opens the Studio, a members-only makerspace, which has an orientation for new users.

records.notes: Youth programs (Teen Photo, Photo in Schools, Partnerships) show no ages, days, cost or enrollment steps, so none are recorded. Membership prices appear with a dollar sign and no currency code. Calendar page has no subscription link. Artist residency pays a $3,000 honorarium, June to November 2026 timing, applications closed when read.

records.name: Tiny Dynamite
records.summary: A Philadelphia theatre company that stages one-hour plays for modest ticket prices in small Center City venues. Volunteers can usher at shows and see them for free.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the volunteer form on the site to join the usher list. Ushers see the show for free and get pizza and a drink. You can also buy a ticket to a show or come to a special party.

schedule.text: Show dates are posted one at a time on the events page. Ushers are called when a spot opens.

locations.label: Show venue: The Drake Theatre lobby
Show venue: The Racquet Club of Philadelphia

cost.text: Tickets are at modest prices, but the pages read did not show exact prices. Ushers see the show for free.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form at tinydynamite.org/volunteer, choosing Ushering, to join the usher list. Then buy a ticket to the next show you want to see.
first_step.basis: The usher form and ticket sales are open to anyone, but no orientation is described and the page does not say how often shows run.
first_step.what_to_expect: Ushers see the show free and get pizza and a drink. The company describes its plays as about an hour long, and the page does not say how long a shift lasts or whether ushers get training.
first_visit_tips: The volunteer form asks for a name, email, and phone; you hear back only when a usher spot opens.
Check the Venues page for where each show is staged, since the site lists no parking or transit notes.
For ticket questions, call the box office at 215-399-0088 or write to boxoffice@tinydynamite.org.

records.notes: Events page names a 2026 Valentine's show and a Jane Austen party by title only, with no dates, so last_sign_of_life keeps the tier 1 month. Contact name from the NCCS 990 e-postcard dataset was dropped because it is not on the group's own site. No accessibility details on any page read.

records.name: Tiny Farm Wagon
records.summary: A mobile art project that builds gardens, runs workshops and holds art events. It works as an art classroom, greenhouse and gallery on wheels, and it cooks plant-based food in a cob oven.
records.what_you_do: Take part in workshops and art events, help build the gardens, or email the project to ask about programs.

schedule.text: No dates are posted. Mother Tongue is described as an annual series of art presentations and workshops, with no dates given.

locations.label: Mailing address (the site does not say where the wagon is)

cost.text: The site does not list costs.

first_step.how: Email tinyfarm.asst@gmail.com, the address on the Contact Us page, to ask about upcoming programs, and sign up for the newsletter on the site.
first_step.basis: Programs are named on the site, but none have dates, sign-up steps or costs, and the volunteer section has no details, so email is the only clear way in.
first_visit_tips: Email before you come, since the site posts no dates or meeting places for its programs.
The Walnut Street address is a mailing address; ask where a program will meet.

records.notes: Program names on the programs page: Philly Youth Story Collective, Mother Tongue, A Room to Write and Rest with Harriett's Bookshop, and a pop-up. No dated item on the site or in one 2026 web search, so status stays probably_active. The Donate and Volunteer sections repeat the same generic copy, so they were not used. Two emails are published: tinyfarm.asst@gmail.com (Contact Us page, used here) and tinyfarmwagon@gmail.com (mistysol page, tier 1). Verify before publishing. The site says the project sits under CultureTrust of Greater Philadelphia.

records.name: Town Watch Integrated Services
records.summary: The City's Town Watch program trains, organizes, and equips residents who want to join a Town Watch group on their block. It also supports CERT, a disaster response program.
records.what_you_do: Observe, document, and report suspicious or criminal activity on your block, and work with district police. Groups also take part in local Police District Advisory Commissions.

schedule.text: Year round, through a Town Watch group on your block

first_step.how: Ask whether a Town Watch group already meets on your block. To ask about joining or starting one, call the office at 215-686-1459.
first_step.basis: The city describes how existing groups get training and certification and gives a form for new groups, but it does not say how one resident joins an existing group.
first_step.what_to_expect: The city's pages describe what Town Watch groups do, not what a meeting is like. Members observe, document, and report, and groups work with district police and local advisory commissions. The city trains and certifies groups, including for CERT disaster response.
first_visit_tips: Call the office before you visit, since the site lists no walk-in hours.
For non-emergency problems, the city's 311 line is linked from the department page.

records.notes: The department page lists an executive director's direct email; it was left out in favor of the office phone. Fees, age or residency rules, background checks and CERT class details are not on the pages read, so none are recorded. The new-group application is a PDF that the site says was released in 2021; its questions were not listed. Dated news on the department page was not used for status, since the tier 1 May 2026 date is newer.

records.name: TreePhilly Volunteer Giveaways (Parks and Recreation)
records.summary: The city's tree program, run by Parks and Recreation, holds tree giveaways around the city, and volunteers sign up for shifts to help run them.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer shift at a citywide giveaway, where you help hand out and plant trees.

schedule.text: Fall giveaways run mostly on weekends: 10 am to noon at neighborhood sites, and 10 am to 2:30 pm at the two citywide sites.

locations.label: Pennypack on the Delaware (northeast citywide giveaway)

cost.text: The trees are free. Only Philadelphia residents can take one, and it must be planted in the ground.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form linked on the TreePhilly page for the next citywide giveaway, at Bartram's Garden on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, from 10 am to 2:30 pm.
first_step.basis: A public sign-up form is linked for the two citywide giveaways. The page does not describe training or what a shift involves.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shifts at the citywide giveaways run 10 am to 2:30 pm, and neighborhood giveaways mostly run 10 am to noon. The page does not say what a volunteer does during a shift, so ask the contact before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Sign up early: the page lists a resident registration deadline about three to four days before each giveaway, and no separate volunteer deadline.
Email treephilly@phila.gov or call 215-683-0217 with questions about a shift.

records.notes: Fall 2026 table lists seven giveaways from Sept 19 to Nov 8. The Sept 19 Pennypack giveaway has already passed. Other dates: Maplewood Mall (Sat Oct 3), Holly Street Community Garden (Fri Oct 9, 4 to 7 pm), Westmoreland Street (Sat Oct 17), Tioga (Sat Oct 24), Tacony Creek Park (Sat Oct 24). Those sites are not added as locations. This record overlaps with treephilly-yard-tree-giveaways (same events and volunteer forms); suggest merging. Shift tasks, training, minimum age and transit are not on the page, so the what_you_do line rests on tier 1 and should be checked.

records.name: TreePhilly yard tree giveaways
records.summary: The City's free yard tree giveaway program gives trees to Philadelphia residents to plant at home, and it needs volunteers to help run its spring and fall giveaway events.
records.what_you_do: Help run a spring or fall giveaway event. The city's pages do not list the tasks volunteers do.

schedule.text: Giveaways run in the spring and in the fall, mostly on weekend mornings.

cost.text: Trees are free, but only Philadelphia residents can take one, and it must be planted in the ground.

first_step.how: Email treephilly@phila.gov or call 215-683-0217 to ask about volunteering at a giveaway, or fill in the volunteer form linked on the TreePhilly page for the Bartram's Garden giveaway on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026.
first_step.basis: Volunteering is open to the public by form or by email, but the city's pages describe no training and no shift tasks.
first_visit_tips: Ask the TreePhilly office what volunteers do at a giveaway before you sign up.
Trees go only to Philadelphia residents who register through the TreePhilly page.

records.notes: Very likely the same program as treephilly (TreePhilly Volunteer Giveaways), with the same events and volunteer forms. Recommend merging into treephilly, or a duplicate verdict, once the orchestrator agrees. Kept as publish here because the batch treats it as its own record. The phila.gov page names the program and a Pennsylvania Horticultural Society Tree Tenders program, but says nothing else. The 2026-09 status date is the tier 1 value and was not re-verified on that page this pass.

notes: Seven records, all verdict publish. Fetches: TILT 6, Tikkun 3, Tiny Dynamite 4, Tiny Farm Wagon 5, Town Watch 3, TreePhilly volunteer 2, TreePhilly yard 1 (24 of 60). One WebSearch (Tiny Farm Wagon 2026): no dated result, so its status stays probably_active. No pages were blocked, and no rate limiting was seen. One mistake: I called a Docs-family tool (guide) that is outside the allowed list. The permission system refused it, I did not retry it, and I used no other tool outside the list. Leads named without a website link were not fetched, since none had their own link and the search budget was spent. TreePhilly volunteer and TreePhilly yard records describe the same program and events; recommend merging, or a duplicate verdict, before publish. Tiny Dynamite: the contact name from the NCCS 990 e-postcard was dropped, because it is not on the group's own site. Town Watch: the department page's direct email for the executive director was left out in favor of the office phone. Tiny Farm Wagon: two contact emails are published; the Contact Us address is used. Tikkun: audience kept at public from tier 1, but the page does not say whether non-members may attend.
